data.name: Philomena
data.gender_notes: Philomena is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Latin philēmōn, meaning lover or friend of God. In Christian tradition, Philomena was a virgin and martyr venerated for her faith. The name Philomena carries the meaning “Friend of tomorrows” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Philomena usually hope their child will grow to embody friend of tomorrows and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes unwavering faith and devotion to God.
data.etymology: Philomena belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Friend of tomorrows.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Philomena total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rosa has its roots in many different cultures and languages. In English, it means 'rose,' the symbol of love and beauty. Romans named their red-haired daughters after the goddess of love, Rosa. In Hinduism, the rose is one of the most sacred flowers, symbolizing love and devotion to the divine.
data.spiritual_significance: Rosa is a name that represents compassion, devotion, and self-love. In Christianity, the rose is a symbol of the Virgin Mary, and Rosa is a name inspired by the Virgin Mary. This name reflects the tender and gentle nature of the mother of God and her love for all God's children.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Philomena means "lover of darkness" in Greek, yet in Christian tradition, she is the saint who symbolizes the hidden mysteries of faith. Her name embodies the paradox of seeking light in the unknown, revealing the depth of divine love and grace.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Philomena was a Greek girl martyred in the 4th century AD. The name Philomena carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Philomena was a Greek girl who was raped and then murdered. Her body was found with a crown of roses, and she was later venerated as a saint.
